precedent.holding: A driver with a light motor vehicle licence needs no separate endorsement to drive a transport vehicle of that class: a transport vehicle or omnibus with gross vehicle weight, or a motor car, tractor or road roller with unladen weight, not exceeding 7,500 kg. Such licences stay valid after the 1994 amendment and the 2001 change to Form 4.

extraction.title_anon: Supreme Court reference from Chhattisgarh: light motor vehicle licence covers light transport vehicles (no amount)
extraction.family_summary: This judgment decides no family's compensation. A three-judge bench of the Supreme Court settled conflicting earlier rulings on whether a driver with a light motor vehicle licence needs a separate endorsement to drive a transport vehicle of that class, such as a goods vehicle or tractor-trailer up to 7,500 kg. In July 2017 it held that no endorsement is needed. The lead appeal came from the Chhattisgarh High Court, which ruled in 2011 on a 2006 appeal; no amounts are stated, and the appeals were sent back to be heard on their facts.
what_mattered: A driving licence is issued by class of vehicle, not by how the vehicle is used: a light motor vehicle licence covers transport vehicles of that class up to 7,500 kg, so no separate endorsement is required.
The Court overruled Prabhu Lal and Angad Kol, and Annappa Irappa Nesaria in part, which had treated such drivers as lacking a valid licence.
No amount was decided: the appeals were sent back to the appropriate bench to be heard on merits.
